title: NZ Defence Force Recruitment 2026: Join the NZDF
metaDescription: NZ Defence Force recruitment 2026: age 17+, citizen or resident, basic training at Waiouru, starting pay, KiwiSaver benefits and how to apply online.
headline: Join the New Zealand Defence Force: 2026 Recruitment Guide

sections.title: The Three Services of the NZDF
sections.content:
The New Zealand Defence Force brings together the Royal New Zealand Navy, the New Zealand Army and the Royal New Zealand Air Force under one command, with around 10,000 regular force personnel plus reserves and civilian staff. Recruits can choose from more than 100 trades, from infantry and combat engineering to aviation, logistics, communications, medical and cyber roles.

The NZDF is actively modernising its recruiting system under its Workforce Strategy, aiming for faster hiring and around 1,500 attestations a year. Entry standards were also relaxed in 2024, with some NCEA Level 1 and Level 2 requirements dropped, so more school leavers can now apply.

sections.title: Who Can Join: Age, Citizenship and Education
sections.content:
You must be at least 17 to apply and 18 by the time you graduate from your recruit course. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens, permanent residents, or hold a current New Zealand residence class visa, and must be able to pass a security clearance that requires a verifiable five-year background history.

You need at least three years of secondary school education and must be medically and physically fit, with no criminal convictions in the previous two years. Officer roles generally require a bachelor's degree, while many soldier, sailor and airman trades accept school leavers with NCEA credits in English and maths.

sections.title: Training, Pay and Benefits
sections.content:
Army recruits complete the All Arms Recruit Course at Waiouru Military Camp, a residential course of around three months that builds fitness, fieldcraft, weapons handling and teamwork before trade training begins. Navy and Air Force recruits complete their own basic courses at Devonport and Woodbourne, followed by specialist training in their chosen trade.

You are paid from day one of training, with under-training salaries around NZD 69,800 a year in many trades. Privates typically earn NZD 44,000 to 51,000 after graduation, rising with rank and experience. NZDF personnel pay at least 3 percent of salary into KiwiSaver and the NZDF matches it with 4 percent, and members receive fully funded life cover of up to NZD 300,000.

sections.title: How to Apply in 2026
sections.content:
Applications are made online through the Defence Careers website, where you can browse every role, check its entry requirements and starting salary, and submit your application. The process then moves through an aptitude assessment, a medical examination, a fitness test and an interview, with a security clearance check running in the background.

Prepare early: gather your identity documents, school records and five years of address and employment history for the clearance, and build your running and strength fitness before you apply. Applying for a trade with strong demand and keeping your application moving quickly gives you the best chance of a place on the next intake.

faqs.q: What is the minimum age to join the New Zealand Defence Force?
faqs.a: You must be at least 17 years old to submit an application and 18 by the time you graduate from your recruit course. There is no single upper age limit for most trades, though officer candidates usually need to commission before their mid-thirties and some specialist roles set their own age caps.

faqs.q: Do I need to be a New Zealand citizen to join the NZDF?
faqs.a: You must be a New Zealand citizen, a permanent resident, or hold a current New Zealand residence class visa. You also need a five-year background history that can be verified for a security clearance, and overseas lateral-entry applications are currently not being accepted for most roles.

faqs.q: How long is basic training in the New Zealand Army?
faqs.a: Army recruits complete the All Arms Recruit Course at Waiouru Military Camp, which runs for around 12 weeks. After that you move into trade training with your chosen corps, which can last from a few weeks to more than a year depending on the trade you selected.

faqs.q: How much do NZDF recruits get paid during training?
faqs.a: Recruits are paid from the first day of training, with under-training salaries around NZD 69,800 a year in many advertised roles. After graduation, privates typically earn NZD 44,000 to 51,000, and pay rises with rank, trade qualifications and time in service.
